title: Brazil’s Economy Is Slowing. Will It Ruin Lula’s Chances?
gist: Brazil's economy is clearly slowing under a 14% Selic, record household debt service (~30% of income) and fading job growth, with Tendências forecasting 1.9% GDP growth in 2026 and ~5% year-end inflation. Yet the slowdown is not seen as decisive: Tendências keeps Lula a slight favorite over Flávio Bolsonaro in a close race likely settled in the October 25 runoff.

insights.claim: Brazil's GDP grew 1.1% in Q1 2026 and only 0.5% q/q in Q2; Tendências forecasts 0.1% average growth in H2 2026 and 1.9% for full-year 2026, down from 2.3% in 2025.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Near-stagnant H2 activity supports further Selic cuts and weighs on Brazilian cyclicals and consumer names.
insights.locator: In the most recent survey from Quaest

insights.claim: Almost half of Brazilians told pollster Quaest that the economy worsened over the last 12 months.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Voter economic pessimism is a live political risk even if not yet decisive.
insights.locator: In the most recent survey from Quaest

insights.claim: A pre-election 'reelection package'—income tax exemptions for workers earning up to five minimum wages, easier debt renegotiation, low-income housing incentives and home renovation support—has propped up consumer sentiment and is masking a weaker underlying economy.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Fiscal stimulus is flattering 2026 data; expect payback and fiscal-credibility questions after the election.
insights.locator: Those numbers would likely be even worse

insights.claim: Brazilian employment growth slowed to 0.9% y/y in July 2026 from 2.4% a year earlier, and real average earnings growth eased to 3.3% from 3.8%, though unemployment remains near historic lows.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Softer wage growth eases services inflation and supports the central bank's easing path.
insights.locator: Even though unemployment remains near historic lows

insights.claim: Brazil created 921,000 formal jobs so far in 2026 versus 1.2 million in the same period of 2025, and informality appears to be stabilizing after 11 consecutive months of contraction.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Momentum fading but no acute deterioration expected near term; a sharper labor break is the key swing factor for the election.
insights.quote: In short, momentum is clearly fading, but there are no signs at this stage of a more acute deterioration in the near term.
insights.locator: Even though unemployment remains near historic lows

insights.claim: Brazil's preliminary August 2026 12-month inflation slowed to 4.2% from 5.5% in April 2025, with goods and services prices posting their first decline in a year and falling food prices driving disinflation since June.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Disinflation through September gives room for rate cuts; positive for BRL duration near term.

insights.claim: Tendências expects Brazilian inflation to re-accelerate in November-December on El Niño-related food price effects and renewed fuel pressures, ending 2026 around 5% versus 4.3% in 2025.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Year-end inflation bump could slow the pace of Selic cuts; watch food and fuel prices into Q4.
insights.locator: That said, inflation is expected to pick up again

insights.claim: Despite gradual cuts, Brazil's 14% Selic rate and a steep, pressured yield curve keep monetary policy firmly contractionary, driving higher delinquency, more emergency credit demand and rising court-supervised restructuring filings.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Credit stress favors caution on Brazilian lenders' asset quality and leveraged mid-caps; judicial recuperação filings are a trackable indicator.

insights.claim: Tendências estimates Brazilian household debt service—interest plus principal—absorbs about 30% of average monthly household income, the highest since the series began in 2004, and expects it to stay broadly stable through year-end.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Record debt-service burden caps consumer spending recovery even as rates fall; bearish tilt on discretionary retail.

insights.claim: Brazilian delinquency is expected to improve modestly by year-end, supported by government debt renegotiation programs for households and businesses.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Mild asset-quality relief for banks into year-end.
insights.locator: As for delinquency, a modest improvement

themes.theme: Election outlook: Lula vs Flávio Bolsonaro

insights.claim: Brazil's economic slowdown, while perceived by voters, is not currently severe enough to decide the October 2026 election; the Supreme Court crisis, misuse of state resources, influence peddling, corruption and US relations are more likely to determine the outcome.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Don't trade the Brazil election purely off macro data; non-economic scandals are the swing variables.

insights.claim: Tendências sees Lula as the slight favorite in a close race likely decided in the October 25 runoff, reflecting opposition weakness more than government strength.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Base case is policy continuity; Brazilian assets may price an opposition win as upside surprise.
insights.quote: That assessment reflects the opposition’s weaknesses more than the government’s strengths.
insights.locator: As a result, Tendências still sees Lula

insights.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro faces high rejection rates, voters appear to fear a Bolsonaro family return more than another Lula term, and other right-wing candidacies are likely to fragment the opposition vote in the first round.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Opposition coordination failure is a structural drag on a market-friendly right-wing victory.
insights.locator: Flávio Bolsonaro faces high rejection rates

insights.claim: If Brazil's economy slows more sharply than expected with clearer labor-market repercussions, the electoral balance could shift toward the opposition.
insights.speaker: ALESSANDRA RIBEIRO
insights.so_what: Monitor monthly formal job creation (CAGED-type data) as the trigger for repricing election odds.
